notes: A pH problem whose cause and whose acceptance criterion both live outside the pH chapter's own answer. Cause and fix are A6.4: ph-low-sc-threshold-01 and ph-table642-low-ionic-01 (below 100 microsiemens per centimetre the water is not conductive enough to complete the circuit and the reading is unstable), ph-low-sc-causes-01 (ionic-strength mismatch with the buffers, larger liquid-junction potential), ph-table642-low-ionic-electrode-01 (fast-responding liquid-filled, Ross combination, or double-junction electrode), ph-kcl-method-01 / ph-kcl-procedure-01 / ph-kcl-bias-01 / ph-kcl-trigger-01 (20 mg KCl into 250 mL raises SC by about 150 microsiemens per centimetre and shifts pH by under 0.01 unit, used only after the normal procedure fails), ph-kcl-other-salts-01. A6.0 carries a handling rule the pH chapter does not: fm-no-stir-below-100-01 / a60-xcut-ph-no-stir-below-100-01 — do not stir a subsample below 100 microsiemens per centimetre. A6.8 carries the acceptance criterion that is itself conditioned on conductivity: mp-form-ph-criteria-06 — plus/minus 0.1 pH unit, relaxed to plus/minus 0.3 when specific conductance is below 75 microsiemens per centimetre. Answer from A6.4 alone and the operator stirs the beaker and holds the wrong tolerance. Predicted rag: the slice's only relevant content is a freshwater pH band of 6.5-8.5 and a baseline conductivity range, neither of which touches low-ionic-strength pH measurement.

turns.content: Headwater stream, very soft water, conductivity sits around 55. The pH reading never settles — it wanders half a unit and keeps creeping. Probe is new. What's actually going on and what do I do about it?

must_contain: identifies water below about 100 microsiemens per centimetre as low ionic strength, which is the cause rather than a faulty probe
explains that the water is not conductive enough to complete the electrical circuit for a stable reading with a combination electrode
names the large ionic-strength difference between sample and buffers and the enlarged liquid-junction potential as contributing causes
recommends a different electrode type for such water (fast-responding liquid-filled, Ross combination, or double-junction)
describes the potassium chloride addition as the sanctioned fix, raising specific conductance by roughly 150 microsiemens per centimetre
states the KCl addition changes the measured pH by less than about 0.01 unit
states the KCl procedure is used only after the normal procedure has been tried and the reading would not stabilise
warns that a subsample below 100 microsiemens per centimetre must not be stirred
must_not: tells the operator to stir or use a magnetic stirrer to speed stabilisation
invents a KCl mass or a resulting conductivity increase not in the manual
attributes the instability to probe failure and stops there
recommends low-ionic-strength buffers for field use without noting they are easily contaminated

turns.content: So when I do my buffer check at this site, how close does it have to land before I stop fiddling with it? Same number as at our estuary pod?

must_contain: states the normal pH calibration acceptance criterion is about plus or minus 0.1 pH unit
states that the criterion is relaxed to about plus or minus 0.3 pH unit when specific conductance is below about 75 microsiemens per centimetre
makes clear the tolerance is conditioned on the conductivity of the water, so the soft-water site and the estuary site are not held to the same bar
notes separately that a post-calibration buffer check should read within about 0.05 pH unit of that buffer's certified value at the calibration temperature
must_not: applies a single pH tolerance to both sites
invents a conductivity threshold other than the one in the manual
confuses the calibration acceptance criterion with the stabilisation criterion for recording a reading
